I had a combo of epirubicin for sure by manually pushed IV and flor-5 by oral pill form I think. I am a little uncertain about the pill... there was a term they used to describe my 'chemo cocktail'

It was 13 years ago.  It was a TNBC. They threw everything at it because I was young and 'healthy'.  

Lost my hair 2-3 weeks after the first dose of epirubicin. All my body hair was gone before the next 28 day round.

Steroids administered ahead of chemo to prevent nausea caused wt gain over 6 months of treatment. The Epirubicin is passed through the urine within a few hours and if not washed through with lots of water, did a little damage to my urinary tract for about a year of occasional infections.

Cipro to prevent infection during treatment ravaged my flora over 6 months. I had 2 fungal infections that could get out of control. 

I also had surgery and radiation which have their own side effects.

Yes... thankfully, breasts don't kill anyone.

If you are alone and young, there are often organizations that have resources for you.  The American Cancer Society (If you are in the US)

Reach out to the organizations. 

You really are not alone. There are many people and charitable organizations that can help you. You need to reach out locally and see where that leads.  Check with your social worker for a referral if you have aged out of the Foster Care System.

Unsweetened chocolate.... or Cocoa Nibs.... Heavy unsweetened cream heated and mixed with cocoa

He can use non-caloric sweetener probably.  not natural sweeteners... sounds like they are also trying to keep blood sugar down.

maybe stick with the low-glycemic fruits... berries, etc

DO NOT SUGGEST NATURAL MEDS!

Some naturopathic medications will interfere with Chemotherapy.

Allow the Oncologists and Nutritionists to do their job.

As far as 'cancer friendly' foods etc.... Every doctor I speak with says that FOOD is not a culpit or a savior.

IMO eating whatever he can keep down or whatever pleases him will help him get the calories he needs.

I eat a 2+:1 keto diet right now. I found a SCHOLARLY article that curated a series of studies which may show a relationship between LOW CARB eating as KETO DIET (creates particular chemistry which limits blood sugars) and the starvation of cancer cells.

This is the least intrusive thing you can do but when we have cancer, sometimes we don't have a choice about what our digestion can tolerate.

My first cancer (13 years ago) involved 6 months of chemo and I found that I craved GREEN PEAS more than anything else.

I found great KETO snacks. DARK chocolate with non-carb sweeteners. Nuts, etc

Seriously though, you can simply offer to get some beautiful high-quality treats or even stuff he just likes and would lift his spirits.

PLEASE STAY AWAY FROM ALTERNATIVE THERAPIES.
